name: Paisley Caves
hook: Ancient Oregon cave feces predate Clovis; the DNA that called them human misclassified some as carnivore.
claim: Researchers recovered coprolites at Paisley Caves, Oregon, that mtDNA identified as human and AMS-dated to about 12,300 14C yr BP (~14,300 cal BP), before Clovis. A 2012 study added Western Stemmed points, at Clovis-age levels, from the same sequence.

claimed_age.label: ~14,300 cal BP (12,300 14C yr BP, AMS on coprolite)
claimed_age.basis: Direct AMS 14C on a coprolite yielding human mtDNA: 12,300 14C yr BP (Gilbert et al. 2008), commonly calibrated to ~14,300 cal BP. Further coprolites and a basketry fragment later dated to a similar range.

accepted_age.label: ~14,000-14,300 cal BP, reaffirmed since 2008
accepted_age.basis: Age reaffirmed without mtDNA: lipid biomarkers on 3 coprolites, dated basketry (12,273±56 14C BP) above coprolite 185, and cut-marked bone below Clovis (Hockett & Jenkins 2013; Shillito 2020).

orthodoxy_at_claim.label: Clovis/Nenana (~13,500-13,000 cal BP) was North America's oldest accepted culture; Monte Verde, Chile (~14.5 ka) was already accepted by 2008.

unambiguous_signal.note: mtDNA indicated human origin, but Goldberg et al. (2009) found micromorphology/FTIR analysis of one dated coprolite hard to reconcile with a human source.

documented_context.note: Excavated in situ by a university field school with recorded stratigraphy, but Poinar et al. (2009) argued the deposits lacked demonstrated stratigraphic integrity at claim time.

multiple_dating_methods.note: Only AMS radiocarbon dating was used to directly date the coprolites at claim; no second independent dating method was applied yet.

multiple_labs.note: By 2012 (four years after the claim), an independent laboratory blind-tested coprolite samples and confirmed human DNA in pre-Clovis specimens.

professional_recovery.note: University of Oregon archaeological field school directed by Dennis Jenkins recovered and recorded the material.

peer_reviewed_report.note: Published as a Report in Science (2008), a leading peer-reviewed journal.

material_accessible.note: Critics Goldberg, Berna and Macphail obtained and independently analyzed one of the actual dated coprolites.

independent_teams.note: Critics (Goldberg, Berna, Macphail) were independent, but the confirming lab was commissioned by proponents and already counted under multiple_labs; no independent corroboration by 2013.

proponent_stake.note: Ordinary university field-school research; no commercial, religious or nationalist motive documented.

objections.text: Micromorphology and FTIR analysis of coprolite 1374-5/5D-31-2 indicated a herbivore, not human, origin; a 2014 steroid-biomarker re-test agreed, conflicting with its mtDNA identification as human.
objections.raised_by: Paul Goldberg, Francesco Berna, Richard I. Macphail; Sistiaga et al. (2014)
objections.outcome_note: Confirmed for this specimen by three methods (2009-2014); Shillito et al. (2020) showed mtDNA can misclassify non-human coprolites as human, and separately confirmed three other coprolites as human by biomarkers.

objections.text: DNA authenticity was questioned: without demonstrated intact stratigraphy, ancient DNA in coprolites might be mobile in cave sediment (leaching) rather than intrinsic to the tested specimen.
objections.raised_by: Hendrik Poinar, Stuart Fiedel, et al.
objections.outcome_note: Shillito et al. (2020) found 6 of 21 mtDNA-typed 'human' coprolites gave carnivore biomarkers, and one Camelidae coprolite dated ~810 14C years apart between fractions, consistent with mobile solutes.

objections.text: In the absence of demonstrated intact stratigraphy and diagnostic artifacts, anomalous carbon-isotope values were said to make the oldest coprolites' radiocarbon dates unreliable.
objections.raised_by: Hendrik Poinar, Stuart Fiedel, et al.
objections.outcome_note: Jenkins et al. (2012) added 100+ AMS dates and pre-Clovis cut-marked bone; Shillito et al. (2020) found basketry (12,273±56 14C BP) stratified above coprolite 185, confirming intact stratigraphy and pre-Clovis age.

status_note: The pre-Clovis age holds: cut-marked bone, dated basketry, and 3 biomarker-confirmed coprolites converge near 12,300 14C BP. But mtDNA misclassified 6 of 21 coprolites as human when biomarkers showed carnivore; hence partial.
what_settled_it: No single event; convergent evidence independent of the original mtDNA method: lipid biomarkers confirming three pre-Clovis coprolites as human, a basketry fragment above dated coprolite 185, and cut-marked bone below Clovis levels (Hockett & Jenkins 2013; Shillito et al. 2020).

timeline.event: Gilbert et al. report human mtDNA (haplogroups A2, B2) from coprolites directly AMS-dated to 12,300 14C yr BP (~14,300 cal BP), predating Clovis.
Goldberg et al. and Poinar et al. publish comments questioning coprolite identification and dating reliability; Gilbert/Rasmussen teams rebut with new data.
Jenkins et al. report 100+ AMS dates, Western Stemmed points at Clovis-age levels, and blind independent-lab DNA confirmation.
Hockett & Jenkins report two cut-marked bones directly dated before Clovis (>13,100 cal BP), independent of coprolite DNA.
Sistiaga et al. re-test the disputed coprolite with steroid biomarkers and confirm a herbivore, not human, origin.
Fiedel publishes continued skepticism about the pre-Clovis claim.
Shillito et al. flag that ancient DNA may be mobile in cave sediment, questioning reliance on mtDNA for coprolite identification.
Shillito et al. confirm 3 pre-Clovis coprolites as human via lipid biomarkers, date a basketry fragment, and flag mtDNA errors in 6 others.
Saban et al. publish a pollen study describing Paisley Caves' dated sequence from 13,000-6,000 cal BP.

decisive_tests.test: Independent-lab lipid-biomarker re-analysis of split samples from the 3 human-confirmed coprolites, using material archived from the original extraction.
decisive_tests.would_show: Whether an outside lab replicates the human biomarker signal on the same specimens.

decisive_tests.test: Second AMS date, at a lab independent of the original program, on the basketry fragment and the two cut-marked bones.
decisive_tests.would_show: Whether the pre-Clovis age holds independent of the Oregon program's own dating.

decisive_tests.test: New excavation or coring by a team independent of the Jenkins program, targeting undisturbed pre-Clovis strata.
decisive_tests.would_show: Whether an independent team can recover further pre-Clovis material at the site.

falsifier: Failure of an independent lab to replicate the human lipid-biomarker signal on split samples of the 3 confirmed coprolites, or evidence that the basketry fragment or cut-marked bones are intrusive into pre-Clovis strata, would overturn this status.

sources.note: Abstract read; reports 12,300 14C yr BP direct AMS date on coprolite with human mtDNA haplogroups A2/B2.

sources.note: Abstract confirms Goldberg et al. argued coprolite 1374-5/5D-31-2 was of herbivore origin; Rasmussen et al. rebut with new genetic data.

sources.note: Abstract confirms the authors stand by their DNA and radiocarbon conclusions.

sources.citation: Jenkins, D.L.; Davis, L.G.; Stafford, T.W.; Campos, P.F. et al. (2012). Clovis Age Western Stemmed Projectile Points and Human Coprolites at the Paisley Caves. Science 337(6091): 223-228.
sources.note: Abstract read; reports 100+ AMS dates, Western Stemmed points at 11,070-11,340 14C BP (Clovis Age, per title), and blind independent-lab DNA confirmation.

sources.citation: Sistiaga, A.; Berna, F.; Laursen, R.; Goldberg, P. (2014). Steroidal biomarker analysis of a 14,000 years old putative human coprolite from Paisley Cave, Oregon. Journal of Archaeological Science 41: 813-817.
sources.note: Metadata confirmed via Crossref; publisher elides the abstract. A Semantic Scholar TLDR indicates a herbivore biomarker finding, consistent with Goldberg et al. 2009 (S4).

sources.citation: Fiedel, S.J. (2014). Did Pre-Clovis People Inhabit the Paisley Caves (and Why Does It Matter)? Human Biology 86(1): 69-73.
sources.note: Only the first page is readable; skeptical framing is plausible but Fiedel's final verdict could not be confirmed. A Wayne State open preprint exists but returned HTTP 403.

sources.citation: Shillito, L.; Whelton, H.L.; Blong, J.C.; Jenkins, D.L. et al. (2020). Pre-Clovis occupation of the Americas identified by human fecal biomarkers in coprolites from Paisley Caves, Oregon. Science Advances 6(29).
sources.note: Full text (EuropePMC) confirms 3 pre-Clovis coprolites human via biomarkers, basketry dated above coprolite 185, and that mtDNA misclassified 6 of 21 'human' coprolites as carnivore.

sources.citation: Saban, C.V.; Herring, E.M.; Jenkins, D.L.; Gavin, D.G. (2023). Late glacial through Early Holocene environments inferred using pollen from coprolites and sediments recovered from Paisley Caves, Oregon. Quaternary Research 116: 78-95.
sources.note: Abstract read; describes a 'well-dated stratigraphy' spanning 13,000-6,000 cal BP; does not address the pre-Clovis levels.

sources.citation: Waters, M.R.; Stafford, T.W. (2007). Redefining the Age of Clovis: Implications for the Peopling of the Americas. Science 315(5815): 1122-1126.
sources.note: Abstract read; narrows the Clovis range to 11,050-10,800 14C yr BP and states pre-Clovis occupation is implied by other evidence.

sources.citation: Shillito, L.; Blong, J.C.; Jenkins, D.L.; Stafford, T.W. et al. (2018). New Research at Paisley Caves: Applying New Integrated Analytical Approaches to Understanding Stratigraphy, Taphonomy, and Site Formation Processes. PaleoAmerica 4(1): 82-86.
sources.note: Abstract read in full; raises whether coprolite DNA may be mobile in sediment rather than intrinsic to the specimen.

sources.citation: Hockett, B.; Jenkins, D.L. (2013). Identifying Stone Tool Cut Marks and the Pre-Clovis Occupation of the Paisley Caves. American Antiquity 78(4): 762-778.
sources.note: Abstract read in full; reports two cut-marked bones from pre-Clovis strata, directly dated before ca. 13,100 cal BP.

sources.citation: Erlandson, J.M.; Braje, T.J.; Graham, M.H. (2008). How Old is MVII?—Seaweeds, Shorelines, and the Pre-Clovis Chronology at Monte Verde, Chile. The Journal of Island and Coastal Archaeology 3(2): 277-281.
sources.note: Abstract read; states most archaeologists by 2008 accepted pre-Clovis settlement before Clovis/Nenana (~13,500-13,000 cal BP); used for orthodoxy_at_claim.

confidence_note: Core chronology (S1, S6, S9 full text) is well verified. S7's abstract is elided (TLDR used); S8 only partly readable. Medium confidence given DNA-reliability complexity.
corrections: Some summaries describe the 2012 Western Stemmed points as pre-Clovis evidence; Jenkins et al. (2012) date them to 11,070-11,340 14C BP and title them 'Clovis Age', not pre-Clovis.
Some accounts place Shillito et al.'s 2020 lipid-biomarker study in Science, by association with Gilbert et al. 2008; it appeared in Science Advances 6(29).
notes: Pre-Clovis evidence now rests on three lines independent of the original mtDNA calls: lipid biomarkers on three coprolites, a basketry fragment above dated coprolite 185, and two cut-marked bones below Clovis levels (Hockett & Jenkins 2013). The 2012 Western Stemmed points are Clovis-age, not pre-Clovis. All this evidence comes from one research program; no independent excavation has occurred. Of 21 re-tested coprolites, 6 that mtDNA called human proved carnivore by biomarkers; one mixed case may reflect coprophagy rather than contamination alone. Fiedel's 2014 final verdict could not be confirmed. No precise coordinates recorded, per heritage-ethics guidance.

open_issues: Removed the single-team/sample-size objection rather than sourcing it (could not verify who specifically raised it in 2009); the underlying 'all pre-Clovis evidence from one program' concern is now covered in status_note and notes instead.

Did not add a separate bioturbation/site-formation mundane-explanation entry given the notes field's length budget; coprophagy is noted as one specific mechanism, and 'contamination' (DNA mobility) is recorded as failure_mode.
